primary_issue: The render does not match the requested shot: there is no crystal wine glass and no visible pouring action (wine stream/splash into glass).
issues: Missing the crystal wine glass hero object (no recognizable glass vessel present).
No pouring action/animation: liquid is not shown streaming into a glass; it reads as a pooled/draped sheet on a rectangular block.
Surface/environment does not match: not a dark wooden table; instead a high-contrast striped/test-pattern platform dominates.
Lighting does not match: candle is visible in-frame (brief wanted off-frame left candlelight) and overall lighting is not convincingly warm/cinematic.
Camera/composition mismatch: not a close-up focused on glass rim + pour + splash; framing is dominated by a black block/platform with large dead areas.
Wine lookdev is not convincing: liquid reads near-black with weak ruby transmission/edge glow expected of red wine.
Fluid behavior/detail is unconvincing: looks overly thick/static with little-to-no readable splash droplets or table drops as requested.
Poor separation/readability: dark liquid blends into the black block; silhouettes/edges are muddy and lack rim definition.
Distracting high-contrast striping causes visual noise/moire-like distraction and pulls attention away from the effect.
suggestions: (Structural) Add/replace geometry with a proper crystal wine glass (thin walls, beveled rim) and stage the pour into the glass. Target: create_geometry.

(Physics/animation) Ensure an emitter/source above frame produces a continuous stream and that the sim/cache is actually baked and advancing; add secondary droplets/splash and a few table drops. Target: setup_physics.
(Scene) Replace the striped platform with a dark wood table material (subtle grain, realistic scale, roughness variation). Target: setup_scene.

(Lighting) Move the candle off-frame left and use it as a warm key (soft amber) with gentle fill from the right; add controlled rim lighting to separate glass/wine from background. Target: setup_lighting.
(Camera) Reframe to a true close-up on the glass rim, incoming stream, and impact/splash zone; reduce dominance of non-hero geometry. Target: setup_camera.

(Wine shading params) The wine appears too opaque/black: reduce volume density (Line 276: 18.0 → ~3–8) and tune wine color toward a deeper ruby (Line 275) so thin regions transmit red while thick regions stay dark. Target: setup_materials.

(Readability) Improve silhouette separation via slightly brighter/specular rim highlights on glass and wine (lighting + material tweaks) so edges read clearly against the background. Target: setup_lighting / setup_materials.
(Remove distraction) Eliminate or heavily tone down the high-contrast striping; if aliasing persists, increase sampling/AA. Target: setup_scene / bake_and_render.
vision_assessment: The image reads like a test scene rather than the requested close-up wine pour. A candle object is visible in-frame, and the main geometry is a black rectangular block sitting on a high-contrast striped platform. The ‘liquid’ appears as a dark glossy sheet/pool draped over the block, with no clear stream entering a glass and no identifiable crystal wine glass present. The lighting is not strongly warm/candlelit in a cinematic way, and the composition is not centered on a glass rim/pour/splash moment. The liquid color is mostly near-black with limited ruby transmission, and there are no convincing secondary droplets or table splashes as described.
